references.text: Psalm 118:22 describes a stone that the builders rejected which has become the cornerstone, which can be seen as a prediction of Jesus' rejection and death, similar to what is described in Matthew 21:39.

Isaiah 5:1-7 contains a parable about a vineyard that God planted but which did not bear fruit, and was therefore destroyed. This resembles the parable Jesus tells in Matthew 21, including the vineyard workers' treatment of the son.

Hosea 12:7 (in some translations Hosea 12:6) mentions God's desire for mercy rather than sacrifice, which can be related to God's desire for justice in the context of the vineyard parable in Matthew 21:39.
The entire parable of the vineyard workers in Matthew 21:33-46, of which verse 39 is a part, serves as an internal cross-reference within the same story.
Mark 12:1-12 tells a similar parable about the vineyard workers, which includes the element of killing the son outside the vineyard.
Luke 20:9-19 also gives a retelling of the parable of the vineyard workers, paralleling the events in Matthew 21:39.
